01Conference basics

Event at a glance

Everything you need to get from the Uber to Booth 436 without a second document.

Who

Cherre + Realpage, one team

The full attendee list is in section 02, and the CREtech audience is described just below. Routing for who to bring in on which conversation is in section 09.

What

CREtech New York

3,000+ attendees, with more than half at executive level and 71% or more at director level or higher. We are a Platinum sponsor, with a turnkey booth, a VIP meeting room, floor decals, and the official lanyard.

Where

Javits Center

429 11th Ave, New York, NY 10001. Booth 436, a 10 by 20 turnkey space. VIP meeting room 1B03.

When

October 20 to 21, 2026

Day 1 is Tuesday, Day 2 is Wednesday. The run of show near the top has the highlights, and the official agenda has every session.

Why

The next chapter of the fall tour

CREtech carries the #NextChapter story forward in New York, with a new wall, a book wall, and a meeting room built like a personal library.

Campaign alignment

Brand activation: #NextChapter · Wall line: There’s More to This Story

Know the audience

CREtech event attendees

Who walks past the booth, and how to pitch the conversation at the right level.

Event overview

Real estate meets the technology shaping its future

  • CREtech New York brings together the real estate industry and the technology ecosystem shaping its future.
  • The audience spans real estate owners, operators, investors, asset managers, technology executives, workplace leaders, and technology companies serving the industry.
Our Main Stage session

Near the end of day one

  • It takes place on the Main Stage near the end of the first day of programming.
  • It is a fast-moving, conversational discussion, not a series of presentations or product pitches.
  • The timing lets us leave the audience with one of the day’s strongest forward-looking conversations.
  • The question is not “How is AI being used in real estate today?” It is “Where is this going, how quickly is it moving, and what should real estate leaders be doing about it now?”
Who will be in the room

A broad range of technical sophistication

  • CEOs and senior business leaders.
  • CTOs, CIOs, and data and engineering leaders.
  • Investment and asset managers.
  • Institutional owners and operators.
  • Workplace and corporate real estate leaders.
  • Technology companies building products for the industry.
How to pitch it

Accessible, not basic

  • Some attendees are deeply technical and already experimenting with sophisticated AI architectures and agentic workflows.
  • Others may primarily know OpenAI through ChatGPT, Google through consumer products or cloud, and Snowflake by name.
  • Do not assume the audience understands the AI stack, but do not over-simplify.
  • The goal is to make complex ideas accessible without making them basic.

03One team, one story

One story, two companies

Realpage and Cherre are telling one story, and the line on our wall is the way in: There’s More to This Story. Everyone attending, across Cherre and every Realpage team on site, says the same thing in the same way.

Our story in one sentence

We help real estate organizations build the trusted data foundation that enables better decisions today and prepares them for AI tomorrow.

The narrative, in order

  1. The industry has changed. More data, faster technology adoption, and AI investment happening all at once.
  2. The challenge is confidence in the data. Organizations already have plenty of it. Trusting it is the hard part.
  3. Trusted data creates better decisions. Quality, connection, and governance are what make analytics and AI usable.
  4. Better decisions create better outcomes. Efficiency, visibility, faster investment decisions, and confident AI adoption.

The conversation, at three lengths

30 seconds

“What do Realpage and Cherre do together?”

Realpage and Cherre bring trusted, connected data to real estate organizations. By improving quality, governance, and visibility, we help clients decide better today and get ready for AI tomorrow.

60 seconds

“Tell me more.”

The industry is racing toward AI, but most organizations are still fighting fragmented systems and manual processes. We solve those foundational problems first, so clients get stronger reporting and more confidence in every decision, while building what they will need for AI.

Three minutes

Start with their problem, not our platform.

Ask: “What operational challenge is taking your team the longest to solve today?” Listen first, understand the business challenge, and only then explain how trusted information supports better decisions.

Five message pillars

Pillar one
Trusted data
Pillar two
AI readiness
Pillar three
Decision Intelligence
Pillar four
Connected operations
Pillar five
Confidence

Messaging do’s and don’ts

Do

Lead with the client’s problem

Business outcomes over technical features, plain language, thoughtful questions, and bring in another teammate when it helps.

Don’t

Lead with product names

Skip straight to a demo, assume everyone knows the org chart, overuse jargon, or treat it like a pitch.

Questions you will hear

Realpage recognized that trusted, connected data has become foundational to the future of AI and real estate technology. Bringing Cherre together with Decision Intelligence strengthens the ability to help clients build confidence in their data while expanding what is possible across the broader Realpage platform. Avoid framing this as Cherre needing rescue, or as Realpage simply buying technology. The story is about creating more value for clients, not one company replacing another.

No. Cherre plays a key role within Decision Intelligence and remains the trusted data foundation behind many of the capabilities on display at CREtech. What has changed is the ability to bring those capabilities to clients as part of a much broader Realpage platform.

AI is creating real opportunity across the industry, but it is only as valuable as the information behind it. The focus here is helping organizations build trusted, connected data so AI produces meaningful, reliable outcomes, not just faster answers.

04On stage

Our programming

Two sessions put our point of view in front of the whole show. Be in the room if you can, and use them as an easy opening on the floor.

Main Stage panel · Tue Oct 20, 4:35 to 4:55 PM ET

Real Estate in the Age of AI: What Google, OpenAI, and Snowflake See Coming

AI is moving past pilots and into the core of how commercial real estate operates. The gap between owners and operators who build a real strategy and those who do not will define the next decade. Attendees leave with a direct read on where AI is headed and what to prioritize now.

Moderator: L.D. Salmanson, CEO and Co-Founder, Cherre
Panelists: Nicole McNamara, AI GTM, Google. Tom Gray, Global Industry ISV and GTM Leader, Snowflake. Taemie Kim, Director of Workplace Data + AI Transformation, OpenAI.

Innovation Stage session · Wed Oct 21, 9:30 to 9:55 AM ET

Analog Trust in an Artificial World

A session on trust in AI: the space between blind trust and skepticism, and how to reach informed confidence and seasoned trust. It covers the infrastructure, data, processes, people, and standards for transparency, governance, and validation that make AI worth relying on.

Speakers: Tyler Christensen, Head of Institutional Client Solutions, Realpage. Kris Kimmerle, VP, AI Risk + Governance, Realpage.

Action

After either session, the best opener at the booth is simple: “Did you catch the panel? What stood out?” Then listen. Trust and AI readiness are the two themes our wall, our story, and these sessions all share.

05Our Next Chapter

The booth experience

Booth 436 continues the library aesthetic from Blueprint, and it supports our fall activation of collecting mini books for our personal “mini” library. The wall is the front cover. The private meeting space is where the story keeps going.

Booth messaging and branding

The outside wall carries three lines against the blue stripes:

  • There’s More to This Story
  • #NextChapter
  • Realpage + Cherre

At Blueprint we were “Cherre, a Realpage company.” Here we are deliberately leading with Realpage to support the brand transition, as we also prepare to attend OPTECH solely as Realpage. Use the wall line as your opener: “There is more to this story, want to hear it?”

The book wall

A wall of books and flowers on the booth itself. It is the curiosity moment. Ask what caught their eye before you say a word about us.

Private meeting space

Our meeting room is designed like a personal library, with the Blueprint library wall inside. This is where conversations get longer, quieter, and more useful.

Check the up-to-date meeting schedule in the shared event tracker (opens in a new tab)

Your library card

Visitors receive their library card once they are inside the meeting room. For Sip, Shop + Celebrate it doubles as the VIP pass, with a stamp for Sip, Shop, and Celebrate. Walk them in, hand it over, and use it to start the next chapter of the conversation.

The library card, front and back

The front reads “VIP Event Access, by invitation only,” with a spot for the guest’s name and three stamps. The back carries the house rules and a QR code to The Private Collection.

By Invitation Only card

This card goes to the guests identified in the “Sip, Shop + Celebrate Invites” tab of the tracker. It carries a QR code that guests show onsite at our VIP event.

General Admission card

We are reserving some General Admission cards with a different QR code. It drives those attendees to a form where they can request a follow-up from a member of our team and ask about a swag item they would like to receive. If they are a qualified lead, we can coordinate shipment.

The client journey, five steps

1

Curiosity

The wall or the arch catches their eye. The goal is to earn a slow-down, not a sale.

2

Engagement

Start a conversation, not a presentation. “What caught your eye?” “What brought you to CREtech this year?”

3

Discovery

Inside the meeting room, once there is rapport, explore the business challenge: what initiative is taking the longest, and how they are thinking about AI.

4

Connection

Think about who else on the team would strengthen the conversation, and make the introduction before they ask.

5

Next step

A demo, an introduction, an executive meeting, a LinkedIn connection. Never let a good conversation just end.

06Your voice matters

Social media playbook

A photo from a teammate will almost always outperform a polished corporate graphic. People trust people, so post as yourself.

Action

The master tracker has the latest on planned posts and themes: open the tracker. Check it before posting if you want to slot into a plan instead of posting cold.

What to share, before, during, and after

Before CREtech

Anticipation

What you are looking forward to, who you hope to meet, why this year matters.

During CREtech

The experience

The wall, the book wall, the library room, team photos, the panel, and client conversations without confidential detail.

After CREtech

Reflection

Your biggest takeaway, a favorite conversation, an industry trend, or a new relationship.

Hashtags and tagging

Every post should include #NextChapter and #CREtechNewYork, and every post should tag @Realpage and @Cherre, no exceptions. Tag clients, partners, speakers, and teammates when they are genuinely part of the story, not to inflate reach.

Brand voice, one example

Instead of

“Excited to showcase our innovative AI-powered solutions.”

Reads like a press release.

Try

“One of my favorite conversations today was about something simple: trust.”

Sounds like a person. Focus on what you learned, not what you sold.

Do’s and don’ts

Do

Share, celebrate, engage

Authentic observations, teammates’ wins, client conversations kept confidential where needed, and comments on other employees’ posts.

Don’t

Confidential detail, badges, pitches

No confidential client information, no photographed badges, no private meeting notes, no announcing deals early, no turning every post into a pitch.

Before you post a photo, ask

  • Is everyone comfortable being photographed?
  • Are names or confidential materials visible?
  • Does this represent the brand well?
  • Does it tell a story?
  • Would you be proud to see it on LinkedIn tomorrow?
  • Did you tag @Realpage and @Cherre?
  • Did you use #NextChapter and #CREtechNewYork?

What counts as a qualified conversation

Not every interaction is one. Generally it means we understand the organization’s current priorities, we identified a business challenge, we know who owns that initiative, we established a logical next step, or we connected with the right decision maker. “Nice meeting you” is not enough. “Let’s continue this next week” is.

Four priorities

One

Strengthen existing relationships

Deepen what already exists through face-to-face time and executive engagement.

Two

Advance active opportunities

Remove obstacles, bring in expertise, validate priorities, agree on next steps.

Three

Identify new opportunities

Not everyone arrives to buy. Stay curious and listen for what emerges naturally.

Four

Strengthen the partner ecosystem

Partner conversations count as much as client ones.

08Lead capture

Badge scanning with Captello

We scan badges with Captello at CREtech. If it did not go through the app, it was not captured.

Requirement

All sales professionals must download the Captello app and scan badges through it

Download and sign in before Tuesday morning, and use it for every conversation worth following up. Questions about access go to Kathy Raissifar.

How it works

Individual access per rep

Each rep scans badges from their own device and downloads their own post-event lead report as a PDF.

Why it matters

Leads are stored per person

Lead data is captured at the individual level. A badge you did not scan yourself is not in your report.

What to expect

No bulk attendee list

CREtech does not share its attendee list in bulk, so scanning is how we build the follow-up list for the conversations we have.

Action

After you scan, add a quick note on what mattered while it is fresh. It makes follow-up faster and keeps the conversation specific.

09Know who to bring in

Discovery + routing

Ask good questions, then bring in the right teammate before the visitor has to ask. Routing below is drafted from titles and tracker roles. Check with the person if you are unsure.

Discovery framework

Understand (“what initiatives is your team focused on this year?”) → Explore (“what is making that difficult today?”) → Clarify (“how are you solving that now?”) → Expand (“who else is involved?”) → Connect (“I would love to introduce you to someone on our team”) → Confirm (“would it make sense to continue this after CREtech?”).

Reading the room

Five visitor types and how to meet each one.
VisitorWhat to do
The explorerLet them look around. Ask what caught their attention. Do not interrupt discovery.
The shopperAsk questions, understand priorities, introduce the right expert.
The existing clientCelebrate the relationship. Introduce colleagues they have not met. Ask what has changed.
The partnerLearn what they are hearing in the market and make the right introduction.
The executiveKeep it strategic. Focus on business outcomes. Bring in leadership early.

10Ownership, not attendance

Responsibilities + expectations

Everyone reading this, whether you are on the floor, managing someone who is, or following along from your desk, owns a piece of what CREtech is supposed to accomplish.

Requirement

Booth 436 must be manned at all times during expo hours. This is not optional. The onsite team coordinates coverage among themselves. If it is busy, do not let anyone stand alone. If it is quiet, that is still someone’s shift, not a reason to leave the booth empty. Whoever is covering stays put, and everyone else can walk the floor, visit partners, attend sessions, support teammates, or capture content.

If you are on the floor

Represent one team

Lead with curiosity, bring in the right expert, scan every badge in Captello, log what you learn, and leave every interaction a little better than you found it.

If you manage someone attending

Set the expectation before they arrive

Make sure they have read sections 05, 07, 08, and 09 before Tuesday, and that they know what a qualified conversation looks like.

If you are reading this at your desk

You are still part of the story

Engage with teammates’ posts, follow up on introductions made on your behalf, and help close what gets logged in Salesforce.

Common mistakes

  • Talking more than the client
  • Explaining products before understanding the problem
  • Trying to answer everything yourself instead of introducing a teammate
  • Rushing to a demo before it is the right next step
  • Forgetting to scan the badge or write down what mattered

Business development is not one team’s responsibility. It is shared by everyone in the room.
